data.narrative:
Realta Fusion is a Series A-stage nuclear energy company that has raised $36M+ to date. Valuation analysis draws on a peer universe of 11 comparable companies across public and private markets: 3 public names (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 8 private firms including Valar Atomics, Helion, X-Energy, and Fuse Energy, representing the same sector and adjacent funding stages.

Two triangulation methods apply. Stage-progression analysis uses total capital raised ($36M) as a proxy baseline and applies a 2.0x multiplier typical of Series A advancement, yielding $72M. Peer-median analysis examines three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables: Valar Atomics at $6.0B (Series B), Nano Nuclear Energy at $808M (Seed), and Fuse Energy at $200M (Series A). The median across this set is $808M, with a range spanning $200M to $6.0B. These methods produce meaningfully divergent signals, reflecting stage heterogeneity and wide valuation dispersion in early-stage nuclear energy.

Triangulated analysis across both methods supports a range of $61M (low) to $929M (high), with a median of $440M. Material uncertainty stems from two sources: the wide spread within the peer set itself, and the fact that stage-progression relies on capital raised as a valuation proxy rather than market-based pricing. Resolution of this range would benefit from comparative revenue multiples or customer traction metrics, neither available in the current dataset.
